identity.title: An ALMA/HST Study of Millimeter Dust Emission and Star Clusters

paper_type_evidence.quote: We combine the *HST* LEGUS database of over 1000 stellar clusters in NGC 628 with *ALMA* Cycle 4 millimeter/submillimeter observations of the cold dust continuum

evidence.quote: NGC 628 is nearly face-on ($i \sim 25$$^\circ$), located at a distance of 9.9 Mpc (cite: Calzetti2015)

question.value: Does the millimeter dust continuum slope (0.87/2.1 mm) in NGC 628 vary with the ages and masses of nearby HST LEGUS star clusters, indicating dust processing by the local radiation field?

evidence.quote: allows us to constrain the spatial variations in the slope of the millimeter dust continuum as a function of the ages and masses of the nearby stellar clusters.

analysis_steps.goal: Detect millimeter sources and measure fluxes

method.value: SExtractor detection requiring 50 contiguous pixels above 2 sigma; keep sources in 80% footprint; noise from randomly placed ellipses; require dual-band centroid match within beam

evidence.quote: with the requirement that each source must have 50 contiguous pixels with flux greater than 2$\sigma$ above the background.

validation.value: Chance alignment test with 10,000 random placements of apertures

evidence.quote: we randomly place our same SExtractor identified source apertures across each image, count how many overlap, and repeat this process 10,000 times.

analysis_steps.goal: Match sources to LEGUS clusters and compute slope

method.value: Find three nearest LEGUS clusters per source using Gaia-registered positions; compute slope S(0.87/2.1 mm) = dlogF/dlogλ

evidence.quote: We identify the three LEGUS star clusters that are projected to lie closest to each millimeter source.

validation.value: Slope uncertainty from difference between summed and stacked (30" cutouts) slopes
